question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s entrenched institutional control and ongoing consolidation of power through anti-corruption purges and loyalty-focused appointments drive the overwhelming trader consensus that he will remain in office through 2026. With the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027, recent developments—including the Beidaihe leadership conclave and preparations for his expected fourth term—show no signs of an imminent exit, as Xi has dismantled term limits, avoided naming a successor, and positioned allies across the Politburo and military. This setup aligns with historical patterns of centralized authority in the Chinese Communist Party, where elite turnover typically spares the paramount leader. While sudden health events or unanticipated internal challenges could theoretically alter the timeline, sustained party discipline and the absence of visible opposition make such shifts unlikely before the congress.
